ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Ludwig van Beethoven Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for progressive hearing loss and constant tinnitus: hearing and depression screening, treatable-cause tests, and a request for otolaryngology consultation. Concerns: He fears his career as a performer will end if his hearing keeps failing; Ringing and buzzing day and night disturb his concentration and sleep; He wants to decide who learns about his hearing and when. [S]
No current medications. The synthetic care plan does not include medication.

list.item: Professional pianist and composer; performs, teaches, and lives on commissions and a patron's yearly stipend; moved to this city from his home town about nine years ago [S]
Lives alone; has avoided parties and gatherings for about two years because he cannot follow conversation and does not want people to know he cannot hear [S]
Communication: German is his first language and he speaks fluent English; understands best face to face, one person at a time, in good light, and wants important details written down [S]
Alcohol: wine with dinner three or four evenings a week, two glasses at most (AUDIT-C 3); no tobacco or other drugs [S]
Noise exposure: hours of daily practice and rehearsal with orchestras; no hearing protection; no firearms or industrial noise; no known lead exposure at work or at home [S]
Wants his hearing loss kept private from employers and colleagues for now [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for progressive hearing loss and constant tinnitus: hearing and depression screening, treatable-cause tests, and a request for otolaryngology consultation
Two-week follow-up and otolaryngology consultation with same-day audiologic evaluation
Five-week review: MRI result, hearing aid fitting, and mood
Three-month review: hearing aid use, tinnitus, communication access at work, and mood
Same-day sick visit for a blocked left ear

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Otolaryngology consultation with a same-day comprehensive audiologic evaluation: pure-tone air and bone conduction, speech audiometry with word recognition, tympanometry, and acoustic reflexes
Tests for treatable causes at intake: blood count, thyroid function, HbA1c, and treponemal antibody; no head imaging for the tinnitus alone
MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium to exclude a retrocochlear cause of the asymmetric loss
Bilateral prescription hearing aids with real-ear verification, a music program, a tinnitus sound generator, and a remote microphone, with audiology follow-up after fitting
Tinnitus education, sound enrichment at night, and cognitive behavioral therapy with a psychologist for tinnitus distress and adjustment; no medication or supplements for tinnitus
Depression monitoring with the PHQ-9 at each visit, a structured safety assessment with a written safety plan and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (text and chat), and safety review at every visit

Communication access on his terms: his communication preferences on the chart, written summaries, captioning and speech-to-text, workplace accommodation when he chooses to ask, hearing loss peer support, and an introduction to the Deaf community and American Sign Language if he wishes
Hearing protection: custom musicians' earplugs for loud rehearsals and limits on unprotected loud sound
Repeat audiogram at six months and with any change; same-week assessment for any sudden drop in hearing
Bilateral hearing aids fitted, verified, and worn at least eight hours a day by three months
Fitted at five weeks with real-ear verification; data logging showed about eleven hours a day at three months
Tinnitus no longer the main barrier to work and sleep, with the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory at least 20 points lower by six months
Tinnitus Handicap Inventory 28, from 58; sleeping through most nights
Communication access he chooses in place for rehearsals, teaching, and meetings by three months
Remote microphone for teaching and rehearsals, live speech-to-text on his phone, and written agendas; he chose to tell his closest colleagues
Hearing protection for loud rehearsals by five weeks
Custom musicians' earplugs with flat attenuation fitted with the hearing aids

list.item: Independent in all activities; composing every day; cannot follow group conversation or soft speech; sits close to the stage to follow theater; has stopped going to social gatherings [S]
Alert, intense, and articulate; leans in and watches faces to follow speech; irritable when asked to repeat himself [S]
Mood low and frustrated, with fear for his career; PHQ-9 score 12 with item 9 scored 0; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1801-04-13: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care. No current thoughts of suicide or self-harm; no firearms at home. Isolation and fear for his career are risk factors, so safety will be reviewed at every visit. A written safety plan was made with him and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline was given, including its text and chat options, which he can use without hearing a voice on the phone [S]
